name: Law firm, accountant or consultant
description: A law firm, accounting or tax office, or a consultancy: the people, the practice areas as services, a price list and clients' questions, with facts about the professional body, fees, the first consultation, insurance and languages.

questions.question: Which professional body are you registered with, and under what registration number?
questions.help: For example the bar, the chamber of tax advisers or of auditors. Your professional rules may require certain details on the website – check which.

questions.question: Which areas do you work in?
questions.help: As clients name them, e.g. "employment law, contracts, debt recovery" or "bookkeeping, payroll, tax returns". Use a protected specialist title only if you hold it.

questions.question: How do you charge for your work?
questions.help: For example "by the hour, fixed prices for standard tasks, monthly flat fee for bookkeeping". The price list holds the amounts.

questions.question: What does a first consultation look like – how long is it and what does it cost?
questions.help: For example "30 minutes free, in person or online" or "paid by the hour like any other work".

questions.question: Are you insured for professional liability? With which insurer, and where does the cover apply?
questions.help: Where such insurance is compulsory, the law may require naming the insurer on the site – check it. Leave it empty if you prefer not to state it and are not required to.

questions.question: In which languages can clients work with you?
Since which year has the practice been running?

audit.message: State your professional body and registration – clients check it, and your rules may require it on the site.
Say how you charge – clients hesitate to call when they cannot guess the cost.
Introduce the people – clients choose a person they will trust with their matter.
Fill in your office address in Business details – clients come to meetings and look for it.
The price list has not changed for a year – check your rates and fixed prices.
Publish a privacy policy page – clients send you confidential personal data; check what your law and professional rules require.

claude: Clients of a law, accounting or consulting practice want to know whether you handle their kind of matter, who will work on it, how you charge and how to make a first appointment – lead with the practice areas, the people and the first consultation. Write calmly and precisely. Never give legal, tax or financial advice on the site: articles explain in general terms, carry their date and say they do not replace advice on a specific case. Never promise outcomes, success rates or savings. Never invent qualifications, titles, specialist designations, registrations, memberships, clients, cases or reviews – ask the owner; never name a client or matter without consent, as confidentiality comes first. Regulated professions may restrict advertising and require certain disclosures – say these should be checked against the professional rules. Forms ask only for contact details and a brief topic, not the confidential facts of a case.
